title: Shared release gave lower effective noise dimension than fixed-count controls in eight selected worm maps
abstract: In eight selected worm brain maps, shared release at a site gave a mean effective noise dimension fraction of 0.544 to 0.689. Fixed-count controls gave 0.560 to 0.749. Observed fractions were 2.8 to 9.0 percent lower than their control means. This result holds under independent and equal-probability release at sites with a shared unit effect on all listed targets. It does not show measured neural noise or a change in representation reliability. We used fixed target counts and site target counts, two randomization chains per map, and longer-run checks. Geometry, release properties and measured activity were not tested.

display.caption: Shared release model. Observed scores and fixed-count control means with central 95 percent reference ranges. Sources have equal weight within a map. Ranges are not animal confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Extends its target-pair concentration and conditional covariance result to standardized effective noise dimension with equal source weights. Reuses the neuron panel, retrieval script and trade code.
